newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa closes lower but July holds support.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa closes lower but July holds support.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures closed down on Thursday, but July managed to hold crucial support at 980 stg, the April 9 low.

May ended down eight stg at 960 stg per tonne and July lost nine to 988. Total volume stood at 6,030 contracts, with July and March tallying the most activity. July grabbed 2,403 trades and March followed with 2,118. All other months traded fewer than 1,000 lots.

In the morning, traders saw mostly outright July selling from various sources, including funds and speculators. Traders said some funds were still trimming long positions while others set new short positions.
In the afternoon, traders said a large European firm sold at least 1,000 March contracts to anchor prices. Some speculated the sales were trade hedges.
But prices held above support as industry buying emerged near the lows, traders said.
But industry buying was limited to small amounts. Traders in Amsterdam said industry buyers were not interested in extending their cover.
Physical traders said Ghana and Ivory Coast were in the cash market over the past week, selling small amounts of nearby cocoa for October/December shipment.
July held its April low, but traders remained bearish in the near term. They said July would have to climb back above 1,020 to erase the past few days' bearish sentiment.

Otherwise, they doubted July could hold 980 much longer, particularly as speculators still seemed net long in New York. Some analysts said the New York market was seriously oversold, but might drift lower to flush out more weak longs before trying the upside again.
July sell-stops were expected in New York near $1,380 and in London below 980.
If 980 broke, traders said, July might quickly drop to next support between 950 and 940, levels not seen since about early March.

The International Cocoa Organization (ICCO) revised up its forecast for 1996/97 cocoa bean production by 93,000 tonnes to 2.715 million tonnes because of larger-than-expected African crops. It estimated the Ivory Coast crop at 1.125 million tonnes.
The ICCO revised down its forecast for 1996/97 world grindings to 2.8 million tonnes, which would still be a record high.
The world deficit this year should be about 115,000 tonnes, it said.
Options activity remained non-existent. No options have changed hands all week.
